opportunity: structsynth measures one function at a time and the layout ledger shares a struct_N only when one reader's claims are a SUBSET of the other's, so two functions that read overlapping-but-different parts of one record get a name each and each is declared to have only the fields its own function touched. On the eight layout builds 23 of the 77 ground-truth records kuna types at all are given more than one struct_N.

typesweep.note: type_match cannot see a record's MEMBERS: a struct_2 * and a struct_3 * score the same, which is why 444 slices move by 0. It does see a record appearing or disappearing, and those 444 slices cover eight projects that happen not to contain that. e2fsprogs does: on e2fsck -O0 the value gives one function a five-field record where it had `void *`, takes the record off three other variables, and turns reconfigure_bool's two `char *` parameters into `unsigned long` -- type_match 0.6667 -> 0.3333 there, the binary's aggregate 201.21 -> 200.88 at an unchanged 12 perfect functions (typesweep --project e2fsprogs --opt O0 --opt O2: 631 functions, perfect +0, 1 worsened, 0 improved). So the option is not metric-neutral by construction; it is metric-neutral over the eight projects the campaign sweep measures. docs/features/structmerge/hunks.md works the class.

hunks.the_one_respelling: grep -O2 sub_7110: the record gains a long member where it had undefined1 filler, so `v1 = a0->field_0x20` (an array member decaying to its address) becomes `v1 = &a0->field_0x20`, the same address with the pointer typed by the member Outside this set the class is larger: e2fsprogs e2fsck -O2 (1,421 functions) changes 56, 54 record-name-only, 2 respelled bodies, 1 of them a declaration-count delta (dict_insert 7 -> 6 declarations, every access at the same address; ext2fs_file_read passes &a0->field_0x14 where filler decayed to a0->field_0x14). Worked in hunks.md.
hunks.scope: the counts below are these ten binaries, not a general rate
hunks.eleventh_binary: e2fsprogs e2fsck -O0 (1,908 functions, 18,080 exported variables) holds a class the ten do not: 185 functions change (175 record-name-only, 9 field-accesses-only, 1 declaration-count delta) and 265 variables, of which 3 LOSE a synthesized record for `void *`, 1 gains one, and reconfigure_bool's two `char *` parameters become `unsigned long` (type_match 0.6667 -> 0.3333). So `siblings` can leave a function worse typed than `off`. The cause is the convergence sweep's redo of every reader of a superseded record, not the union: `--option protoorder lock` leaves not one variable on the binary changing type. Worked in hunks.md.
hunks.merged_mint_fallback: lookup_or_mint falls through to the reader's own claims when the union will not mint, so a declined union never leaves a reader untyped where `off` types it. Measured inert on the corpus: KUNA_STRUCTMERGE_TRACE=1 over e2fsck -O0 plus twelve campaign binaries (ls/sort/du/fmt -O0 and -O2, grep, gzip, diff, tar, find, useradd, bzip2) traces 37,571 candidates and 0 mint failures, so the typesweep and layoutscore numbers above are unchanged by it.

jobs: a --jobs N worker answers through the shard replay, which records the layout each request measured, so it never merges and a sharded run behaves as off -- the same divergence structsynth already has. Verified: coreutils fmt -O2 with --jobs 2 is byte-identical with the option off and with siblings.
